entities.summary: Sonia Delaunay was a French artist born to Jewish parents, who spent most of her working life in Paris. She was born in the Russian Empire, now Ukraine, and was formally trained in Russia and Germany, before moving to France and expanding her practice to include textile, fashion, and set design. She was part of the School of Paris and co-founded the Orphism art movement, noted for its use of strong colours and geometric shapes, with her husband Robert Delaunay and others. She was the first living female artist to have a retrospective exhibition at the Louvre in 1964, and in 1975 was named an officer of the French Legion of Honor.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a co-founder of the Orphism art movement and a prominent figure in the School of Paris, Sonia Delaunay's work had significant regional impact on modern art. Her textile designs and fashion contributions also influenced the development of modernist art and design.
